evidence: Ter. Eun. 3.5.47, as cited by Lewis & Short: cape hoc flābellum, et ventulum huic sīc facitō

phrases.latin: Cape hoc flābellum, et ventulum mihi facitō.
phrases.english: Take this fan and make me a little breeze (after Terence).

phrases.latin: Sī furnus tuus flābellō āëra calidum circumagit, vīgintī gradūs dētrahitō.
phrases.english: If your oven has a fan that circulates hot air, take off twenty degrees.

sources: Lewis & Short: flabellum

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. fly-swatter, mouse-trap, vase, lamp: candlestick, lamp: chandelier, lamp: flashlight. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, supplied PDF (printed page numbers): pp. 122, 123, 313, 316, 403.
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours, after Terence.
Theodōrus et pater: Culīna Theodōrī, the recipe book that goes with the libellī (Ad Libellōs I–VII); examples marked “Culīna Theodōrī” quote it word for word.
